## How to add an equation of state {#sec-ch02-new-eos}

A new equation of state needs a C++ implementation and a factory entry. Changing the deck alone cannot add
one: the factory rejects an unknown `type`. Start with the dry ideal-gas implementation when the new model
uses the same state layout; the existing choices and conversion keys are listed in @sec-ch02-interface.

1. **Implement the class in `src/eos/`.** Follow
   {{< code src/eos/ideal_gas.hpp IdealGasImpl >}}: derive from
   `torch::nn::Cloneable<MyEOSImpl>` and `EquationOfStateImpl`, provide `reset()`, expose the inherited
   `forward`, and declare `TORCH_MODULE(MyEOS)`. Pass the options and parent to the base constructor;
   it requires a `HydroImpl` parent ({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::EquationOfStateImpl >}}).
2. **Implement the thermodynamic contract.** Override `compute(std::string ab,
   std::vector<torch::Tensor> const& args)`. The base implementation throws. For a dry-gas starting point,
   retain all seven branches of {{< code src/eos/ideal_gas.cpp IdealGasImpl::compute >}}:
   `W->U`, `U->W`, `W->I`, `W->T`, `UT->I`, `W->A` and `WA->L`. Conversions accept an optional output
   tensor as the second argument; otherwise they allocate with `empty_like`. Temperature, internal-energy
   density, adiabatic index and sound-speed results have the cell shape, without the state-row dimension.
   Preserve the state layout and metric conventions in @sec-ch01-layout, including ghosts; follow the limiter
   calls in {{< code src/eos/ideal_gas.cpp IdealGasImpl::_prim2cons >}} and
   {{< code src/eos/ideal_gas.cpp IdealGasImpl::_cons2prim >}}. Those calls can modify their input tensors.
   Keep tensor allocations on the input dtype and device, as the existing `empty_like` and `ones_like` calls do.
3. **Supply model-specific properties.** Implement `nvar()`, `species_weight`, `species_cv_ref` and
   `specific_heat_cv` as in `IdealGasImpl`. Review `internal_energy_offset` and `species_enthalpy` for a
   constituent model: their base defaults are zero and an undefined tensor, respectively
   ({{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.hpp EquationOfStateImpl >}};
   {{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::internal_energy_offset >}}).
   These defaults do not establish consistency for a new model; use @sec-ch02-consistency.
4. **Register and select it.** Include the new header and add a branch to
   {{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateImpl::create >}}. For example, this is the existing
   ideal-gas registration with only the proposed name and holder substituted:

   ```cpp
   } else if (opts->type() == "my-eos") {
     return p->register_module(name, MyEOS(opts, p));
   ```

   Select it in a complete input deck with the fragment below. `my-eos` is a proposed name, not a shipped
   option. The parser reads this string; its default remains `moist-mixture`. New parameter keys also need
   options, parsing and admission to `check_keys` in
   {{< code src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp EquationOfStateOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}.

   ```yaml
   dynamics:
     equation-of-state:
       type: my-eos
   ```

The smallest implementation exercise is to copy `ideal_gas.hpp` and `ideal_gas.cpp` to new names, rename
`IdealGasImpl`/`IdealGas` throughout, and add the factory branch above before changing any thermodynamics.
Reconfigure and rebuild: [`src/CMakeLists.txt:35-40`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/CMakeLists.txt#L35-L40)
collects `eos/*.cpp` at configure time. This recipe preserves the existing dry-gas closure; it is not a
validated new physical model. Check conversion round trips, the temperature/internal-energy identities and
sound speed before using a changed closure. Runtime validation of this proposed copy is not provided here.
